question: How is biological growth (生長) defined in multicellular organisms?
options: A temporary increase in body mass caused solely by water intake
An irreversible increase in the size and dry mass of an organism resulting from cell division and cell enlargement
The specialization of unspecialized cells into specific tissues
The movement of organisms from one habitat to another

question: What is cell differentiation (細胞分化) during development?
options: The rapid mitotic division of a zygote without any increase in total volume
The process by which unspecialized cells become specialized in structure and function to perform specific roles
The breakdown of stored food reserves in cotyledons
The elongation of plant cells by absorbing water into vacuoles

question: Dry mass (乾重) is the most accurate parameter for measuring true biological growth because it excludes fluctuations in water content inside the organism.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: What is a major disadvantage of using dry mass to measure the growth of a population of plants?
options: Dry mass fluctuates wildly depending on when the plant was last watered.
Measuring dry mass requires heating organisms in an oven until all water evaporates, which kills the organisms and prevents repeated measurements on the same individual.
Dry mass cannot be measured in kilograms or grams.
Dry mass only measures inorganic mineral content.

question: Which parameter is most practical and non-destructive for monitoring the growth of a human infant over several years?
options: Dry mass / 乾重
Fresh mass (body weight) and height (length) / 鮮重和身高
Total surface area of skin / 皮膚總表面積
Volume of water displaced / 排水體積

question: In flowering plants, primary growth (初生生長) occurs at the apical meristems (頂端分生組織) located at the tips of shoots and roots, resulting in an increase in length.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Which sequence correctly represents the three regions of growth behind a root tip, starting from the tip and moving backwards?
options: Region of differentiation → Region of elongation → Region of cell division
Region of cell division → Region of elongation → Region of differentiation
Region of elongation → Region of cell division → Region of differentiation
Region of cell division → Region of differentiation → Region of elongation

question: What protects the delicate apical meristem at the tip of a growing root as it pushes through the soil?
options: Waxy cuticle / 角質層
Root cap / 根冠
Root hairs / 根毛
Casparian strip / 凱氏帶

question: In the region of elongation (伸長區) of a plant root or shoot, cells elongate primarily by absorbing water into numerous small vacuoles, which merge to form a large central vacuole.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: In a classic experiment where equally spaced ink marks are drawn along the radicle of a germinating bean seedling, which region shows the greatest increase in distance between marks after 2 days?
options: The very tip covered by the root cap
The region just behind the root tip (region of elongation)
The upper region near the seed coat where root hairs are mature
All regions elongate equally

question: What is secondary growth (次生生長) in woody dicotyledonous stems and roots?
options: Increase in length caused by apical meristems
Increase in thickness (girth) caused by lateral meristems such as the vascular cambium (維管形成層) producing secondary xylem and secondary phloem
Formation of adventitious roots from leaves
Growth of lateral buds into flowers

question: Annual rings (年輪) visible in the cross-section of a woody tree trunk are formed by seasonal variations in the size of secondary xylem vessels produced by the vascular cambium.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Which type of germination occurs when the cotyledons are carried above the soil surface by the elongation of the hypocotyl (下胚軸), as seen in French beans?
options: Hypogeal germination / 留土萌發
Epigeal germination / 出土萌發
Vegetative propagation / 營養繁殖
Parthenocarpy / 單性結實

question: In hypogeal germination (留土萌發), such as in broad beans or maize, which part elongates to push the plumule out of the soil while the cotyledons remain underground?
options: Hypocotyl / 下胚軸
Epicotyl / 上胚軸
Radicle / 胚根
Testa / 種皮

question: In annual flowering plants, a typical growth curve plotted using dry mass over time is S-shaped (sigmoid curve / S形曲線), ending with a slight drop in dry mass during senescence and seed dispersal.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Which characteristic distinguishes growth in mammals (such as humans) from growth in woody perennial plants?
options: Mammals grow only at apical meristems at the tips of limbs.
Growth in mammals occurs throughout the entire body (allometric growth) and stops upon reaching adulthood, whereas plants show localized meristematic growth throughout life.
Mammals grow in steps by moulting an external skeleton.
Different parts of a human body grow at the exact same rate from birth to adulthood.

question: During which two periods of human life does the fastest rate of growth (growth spurts) occur?
options: Early childhood (ages 4–7) and old age (ages 65–75)
Infancy (first 2 years after birth) and adolescence/puberty (roughly ages 11–16)
Middle adulthood (ages 30–45) and late adulthood (ages 50–60)
Only during the last month before birth

question: In humans, girls generally enter their adolescent growth spurt about 1 to 2 years earlier than boys, though boys usually continue growing longer and reach a greater average adult height.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Which part of the human body grows very rapidly during infancy and early childhood, reaching nearly 90% of its adult size by age 6?
options: Reproductive organs / 生殖器官
Head and brain / 頭部和腦
Legs and arms / 四肢
Skeletal muscles / 骨骼肌

question: How do arthropods such as insects and crabs grow despite having a rigid, non-living chitinous exoskeleton (外骨骼)?
options: Their exoskeleton stretches continuously like elastic rubber.
They exhibit intermittent growth by periodically shedding their old exoskeleton (moulting / 蛻皮) and expanding rapidly before the new cuticle hardens.
They dissolve their exoskeleton internally every night.
They only grow during the adult stage after wings form.

question: Immediately after moulting, an insect takes in air or water to expand its body volume while the new exoskeleton is still soft and pliable.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Which characteristic of apical meristem cells (頂端分生組織細胞) enables them to divide rapidly?
options: Large central vacuoles and thick lignified cell walls
Small size, thin cellulose cell walls, dense cytoplasm, and large prominent nuclei
Presence of numerous chloroplasts and thick waxy cuticles
Hollow dead lumens with perforated end walls

question: Unlike most mature animal cells, many differentiated plant cells retain the ability to dedifferentiate and grow into a whole new plant under suitable tissue culture conditions.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: [REGIONS OF ROOT GROWTH] A longitudinal section of a young dicotyledonous root tip reveals three distinct zones behind the root cap. 1) Name these three zones in order from the root tip upwards and state the main cellular process occurring in each. 2) Explain how cells in the middle zone achieve rapid increase in length.
